title: Shared-origin storage chooses the federation token endpoint and an unsigned ID token is saved
description: The checked-in Pages profile is shared_origin_demo on https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io. Boundary 13 and storage-ownership.ts state that a path is not origin isolation, so another document on that origin can write the OpenSesame localStorage key. completeSignInDefault posts the authorization code, redirect URI, client id, and PKCE verifier to pending.tokenEndpoint and never substitutes the compiled issuer endpoint. readIdentity then decodes the returned JWT and checks iss, aud, and exp, but not the signature, on the assumption that the token came from the issuer token endpoint. decodeJwtEnvelope accepts an alg-none header only when every segment, including the signature, is non-empty base64url; an empty signature segment is rejected, and a non-empty unchecked segment is accepted. requireActiveUpstreamSession calls pending.sessionCheckEndpoint when that field is set, and any result other than HTTP 401 is success, including a missing endpoint. A same-origin writer can therefore rewrite a live pending record so an in-progress code and verifier are sent to an attacker server, and can plant a record that stores an unsigned token with iss https://shoo.dev when the attacker check does not return 401. saveSession writes that identity even when jwksUri is omitted, but loadSession then clears the row because identityFromJwt requires a string jwksUri. With jwksUri set, loadSession returns the forged subject. The compiled mock issuer http://127.0.0.1:9090 has no session check, so the same unsigned-token path saves a mock session after only the attacker token response. Sealing does not stop the write: a value that is not an at-rest seal is returned as plaintext, including after a sealed value is overwritten. Planting opensesame:federation:session directly also makes loadSession return an unsigned Shoo subject with no token POST; that write is the documented shared store. The additional crossing is the callback code, which is not in shared storage, being posted with the verifier to the storage-chosen token endpoint before the session check. The comparable static-auth Shoo passthrough pins https://shoo.dev/session/check and accepts only status active; app-core does not share that fail-closed pin. The ambient exchange has the same unbound tokenEndpoint and jwksUri shape, but ambient SSO returns null unless that capability is installed, and that path was not executed. An orgSlug record skips the issuer allowlist and does not save a federation session.
root_cause: The PKCE pending record is trusted for tokenEndpoint and sessionCheckEndpoint at exchange time, and readIdentity skips signature verification because it assumes that stored URL is the trusted issuer endpoint. The session-check backstop uses the stored URL and fails open on every status except 401.
intended_behavior: The code and PKCE verifier are posted only to the compiled token endpoint for a trusted issuer, or to an endpoint whose origin is pinned to that issuer. The ID token is accepted only after a signature check against that issuer's keys or after an explicit active result from the compiled session-check URL. Another document on a shared origin cannot choose those URLs or install a federation session.

trace.description: Lower-trust entry. The PKCE record is read from origin localStorage key opensesame:federation:pkce, then sessionStorage. On the shared github.io origin that store is writable by every document of the account, not only this app path.

localStore().getItem goes through sealedWebStorage. A value that is not an at-rest seal is returned as plaintext, so a same-origin writer does not need the at-rest key to plant the pending record. Overwriting a sealed value with plaintext is also returned as plaintext.
The JSON is overlap-cast with no check of tokenEndpoint, sessionCheckEndpoint, or jwksUri. A numeric createdAt older than ten minutes is stale. A missing createdAt is not aged out.

The authorization code, redirect_uri, client_id, and code_verifier are POSTed to pending.tokenEndpoint as application/x-www-form-urlencoded with credentials omitted. The URL is not replaced with the compiled upstream token endpoint.

The ID token is decoded and checked for issuer, audience, expiry, and pairwise_sub or sub. The signature is not verified. Issuer https://shoo.dev and http://127.0.0.1:9090 are both in TRUSTED_UPSTREAMS, so an unchecked payload with one of those iss values passes when the envelope has three non-empty base64url segments.

The session-check URL is pending.sessionCheckEndpoint or, if absent, the compiled URL. A missing URL, a transport error, or any HTTP status other than 401 returns success. The mock issuer has no compiled check.

When orgSlug is absent, saveSession writes the identity, including the attacker-supplied pairwise subject and the raw ID token, through writeFederationSessionJson. loadSession later accepts that stored token without a signature check when jwksUri is a string, and clears the row when it is not.

evidence.description: The checked-in Pages profile is shared_origin_demo, with canonicalOrigin https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io and headerSecurity false on the following lines of the same object.

Boundary 13: unrelated content on the same origin shares one browser trust boundary, and a path is not origin isolation. The shared-origin demo stays restricted; this is calibration, not a control that pins the token endpoint.
The app states that a github.io origin belongs to every GitHub Pages project site of the account and that origin storage is not divided by path.

mayPairLocalAuthority is false when resolveDeploymentProfile returns shared_origin_demo. The sandbox observed that result for the checked-in origin and profile. Shoo sign-in is not removed with pairing.
The compiled Shoo upstream has token endpoint https://shoo.dev/token and session check https://shoo.dev/session/check. Exchange does not use these when the pending record supplies its own URLs.

TRUSTED_UPSTREAMS includes the mock issuer http://127.0.0.1:9090 with a token endpoint and JWKS URL and no sessionCheckEndpoint. The comment says tests name it explicitly; the production allowlist still contains it.
requireActiveUpstreamSession returns success for every HTTP status other than 401. A transport error returns at the catch above, and a missing endpoint returns before the fetch.
The comment above readIdentity says the signature is not re-checked because the token arrived over TLS from the token endpoint, citing OIDC Core 3.1.3.7.

readStoredSessionSync, used by loadSession, does not check the signature. Its JWT path requires a string jwksUri. The Shoo payload that omits jwksUri was written by saveSession, then loadSession returned null and cleared it. The same payload with a jwksUri string made loadSession return pairwise subject forged-subject.

unwrap decrypts the origin at-rest data key with the IndexedDB wrapping CryptoKey. That database is origin-scoped, so a same-origin script can use the key and rewrite a sealed value as well. The executed path did not need this, because plaintext is accepted.
Calibration only: the static-auth Shoo passthrough posts to the pinned https://shoo.dev/session/check URL and requires status active. app-core federation does not share that control.

The ambient variant POSTs the code and verifier to transaction.tokenEndpoint and then verifies with transaction.jwksUri. That path was read in source and was not part of the sandbox execution, because the default ambient seam returns null when ambient SSO is not installed.

conditions.description: The deployment uses the checked-in shared_origin_demo profile, or any other origin where a second document can script the same origin. mayPairLocalAuthority is false there. A dedicated origin would require script execution inside the app origin, which this profile does not require.

The attacker is another page or script on that origin, such as a sibling GitHub Pages project or the account's user-site path. That page can read and write origin localStorage and can open the origin IndexedDB. A page on a different origin cannot.

For code theft, beginSignIn has stored a live pending record and the attacker rewrites tokenEndpoint before the callback. For a durable forged session through this exchange, the planted record includes a string jwksUri; omitting it still sends the code, but loadSession then clears the saved row. createdAt must be a recent number or omitted; createdAt 0 is older than ten minutes and was refused.

The person loads the OpenSesame document on that origin with the callback code and state. Code theft also needs a sign-in to be in progress. Session forgery needs that document to process the callback query the attacker can open.

execution.attacker_perspective: A same-origin document writes the federation pending record so its issuer is a compiled trusted issuer and its token and session-check URLs are an attacker server. When OpenSesame completes the callback, it sends the code and PKCE verifier to that server and, if the server returns an unchecked token and the session check does not reject with HTTP 401, stores that token as the federation session when jwksUri is a string.
payloads: JWT header {"alg":"none","typ":"JWT"}, payload {"iss":"https://shoo.dev","aud":"origin:https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io","exp":4000000000,"pairwise_sub":"forged-subject","email":"forged@attacker.example"}, and a non-empty unchecked signature segment

{"upstreamId":"mock","issuer":"http://127.0.0.1:9090","verifier":"verifier-mock","state":"state-1","tokenEndpoint":"https://attacker.example/token","jwksUri":"http://127.0.0.1:9090/jwks","clientId":"origin:https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io","createdAt":<Date.now()>} with the same unchecked token shape and pairwise_sub mock-forged
instructions: Bundle the real completeSignIn, readIdentity, requireActiveUpstreamSession, and sealed web-storage read with esbuild. Do not contact the network. Point fetch at a local stub that records the URL, method, and body and returns an unchecked ID token or an HTTP status.

Install a host whose securityProfile is the checked-in shared_origin_demo object, whose page origin is https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io and base path is /OpenSesame/, and whose local storage is an in-memory map. Defaults already leave remote Identity API and operator providers empty.

Write the Shoo pending payload as plaintext under opensesame:federation:pkce, once without jwksUri and once with a string jwksUri, set the page search to ?code=attacker-code&state=state-1, and call completeSignIn, then loadSession.

Repeat with the same attacker token endpoint and no sessionCheckEndpoint override so the compiled https://shoo.dev/session/check stub returns HTTP 401. Then repeat with the mock issuer payload and no session check. A Shoo payload with createdAt 0 is a negative check only. Also overwrite a sealed pending value with plaintext, and separately write opensesame:federation:session directly.

Run that bundle through sandbox-run.sh with node --max-old-space-size=128. The sandbox allows PATH, HOME, TMPDIR, LANG, and LC_ALL, blocks external network, and sets a 1 GiB virtual-memory cap and a 25 second timeout. The script printed its results; process teardown in this sandbox then aborted on a node bundled-root-certificate assertion.
execution.observed_result: shared_origin_demo resolved for https://tyler-r-kendrick.github.io and mayPairLocalAuthority was false. Plaintext under opensesame:federation:pkce was returned by the sealed reader, including after a sealed value was overwritten. The Shoo payload with no jwksUri POSTed to https://attacker.example/token with grant_type, code attacker-code, the redirect URI, client id, and verifier, then POSTed to https://attacker.example/check, and saveSession wrote issuer https://shoo.dev, pairwise subject forged-subject, and email forged@attacker.example. The following loadSession returned null and removed that row. The same payload with jwksUri https://shoo.dev/.well-known/jwks.json left loadSession returning forged-subject. With the compiled Shoo session check left in place, the token POST still went to https://attacker.example/token and HTTP 401 from https://shoo.dev/session/check raised login_required and left no saved session. The mock issuer saved pairwise subject mock-forged after only the attacker token POST, and loadSession returned it. The same Shoo payload with createdAt 0 was refused as an expired sign-in and saved nothing. An empty signature segment was rejected as invalid_token. A direct plaintext write of opensesame:federation:session, with no token POST, made loadSession return pairwise subject direct-plant. Redemption of the code at the real Shoo token endpoint was not attempted.

remediation.strategy: At exchange time, ignore tokenEndpoint and sessionCheckEndpoint from storage when the issuer has compiled endpoints. Post the code only to that compiled token endpoint, or, for an operator issuer with no compiled endpoint, to a URL whose origin equals the issuer origin. Call only the compiled Shoo session-check URL and accept the sign-in only on an explicit active result. Where no compiled check exists, verify the ID token signature against the compiled JWKS or refuse that issuer outside tests. Do not treat the loopback mock issuer as a production session issuer without one of those checks. Apply the same origin pin in the ambient exchange before verifyBrowserIdTokenClaims; that path was not executed here.

likelihood.reason: The shipped Pages profile is the shared github.io origin, so another document already on that origin can write the pending record. A page on a different origin cannot. Publishing or scripting that origin still requires a foothold on the account, and stealing a real code also needs a sign-in inside the pending window.

impact.reason: The app sends the authorization code and PKCE verifier to the attacker URL before the session check runs. That code is not in shared storage. The body is what a redemption at the real token endpoint requires; redemption itself was not observed. With a string jwksUri the app also keeps an attacker-chosen pairwise subject as the Shoo or mock federation session. A direct write of the session key can plant that local subject without the exchange, and the forged token does not decrypt an existing end-to-end vault.

confidence.reason: The real completeSignIn path was executed in the sandbox for the Shoo payload with and without jwksUri, for the compiled Shoo check returning HTTP 401 after the attacker token POST, and for the mock issuer. Issuer trust for those two issuers comes from TRUSTED_UPSTREAMS, and the shared-origin precondition is the app's own storage rule for this profile.

title: Exported custom-scheme handlers skip invocation policy before wallet operations
description: MainActivity is exported, declares no android:permission, and is BROWSABLE for openid-credential-offer and haip-vci with host *. Its https VIEW branch calls validatePlatformInvocation and forwards only the returned protocolUri into launchOpenID4VCIProvisioning or into OpenId4VpActivity. That policy admits only an associated https link with one of request_id, user_code, or a public https request_uri, and it rejects credential_offer, token, code, password, secret, any other parameter, and private, loopback, or link-local request hosts. The custom-scheme branch never calls it: both issuance schemes pass intent.data.toString() straight to launchOpenID4VCIProvisioning. The function cannot be applied to that raw string, because it requires the https authenticator origin and fails closed as UnverifiedInvocationOrigin before any host check; the missing control is an equivalent check of the offer before the handoff. Exported OpenId4VpActivity is a second permissionless BROWSABLE entry for openid4vp, haip-vp, and mdoc, subclasses UriSchemePresentmentActivity, and never calls validatePlatformInvocation. The https OID4VP branch shows that activity's VIEW data is the presentment protocol URI. usesCleartextTraffic false and the provisioning client's followRedirects false do not inspect the initial host or an inline credential_offer, and requireFreshUserVerification is not called on these paths. The iOS WalletView adapter uses the same https-versus-custom-scheme split; that calibrates the pattern and does not show Multipaz refusing a private or inline offer. ADR 0058 documents both associated https links and these schemes as handoff channels. Whether Multipaz then fetches a private credential_offer_uri or request_uri, or accepts an inline credential_offer, is not in the repository.
claimed_root_cause: Custom-scheme VIEW handlers on exported activities pass attacker-controlled intent data into OID4VCI provisioning or OID4VP presentment without the private-URI and forbidden-parameter checks that the https branch applies through validatePlatformInvocation.

trace.description: MainActivity is exported with no android:permission and this BROWSABLE VIEW filter registers openid-credential-offer with host *; haip-vci is the next data element in the same filter.
openid-credential-offer and haip-vci take uri.toString() with no call to validatePlatformInvocation and no private-host or forbidden-parameter check.
That raw offer string is passed to launchOpenID4VCIProvisioning. The https branch reaches the same call only with invocation.protocolUri after validatePlatformInvocation.

evidence.description: The https branch calls validatePlatformInvocation with the configured origin and later forwards only invocation.protocolUri.
The openid-credential-offer and haip-vci branch does not call validatePlatformInvocation before the provisioning handoff.
OpenId4VpActivity subclasses UriSchemePresentmentActivity, returns WalletRuntime.presentmentSource, and has no invocation-policy call.
OpenId4VpActivity is exported and declares no android:permission.
The OpenId4VpActivity VIEW filter is BROWSABLE and registers openid4vp with host *; haip-vp and mdoc follow on the next lines.
validate_link accepts only an https URL whose origin is the authenticator origin, so a custom-scheme string never reaches the later parameter or host checks.
On an https invocation the policy rejects credential_offer, token, code, password, and secret, then rejects any parameter other than request_id, user_code, or request_uri.
When allow_private_request_uris is false, which new() hardcodes, a private or loopback request URI is rejected before a protocol URI is built.
The provisioning HTTP client disables redirect following. That does not validate the initial offer host or refuse an inline credential_offer.

blockers: This environment has no Android emulator or device, so an explicit or browsable VIEW intent was not delivered to MainActivity or OpenId4VpActivity and no dummy listener was contacted.

org.multipaz:multipaz:0.100.0 and org.multipaz:multipaz-compose:0.100.0 are not in the repository or a local Gradle cache, so it is not source-visible whether launchOpenID4VCIProvisioning or UriSchemePresentmentActivity fetches a private credential_offer_uri or request_uri, accepts an inline credential_offer, or returns before any network or credential operation. That library behavior is the decisive effect.

validation_plan.local: On an emulator, install a debug build with opensesameWalletBackendUrl set to a dummy https origin and opensesameInvocationHost set to a non-production hostname. Use no production backend, store signing key, or real credential. If WalletRuntime.initialize throws before handleIntent, record that and stop; the run is inconclusive. From a second app, send explicit ACTION_VIEW intents and stop at the boundary: MainActivity with data openid-credential-offer://?credential_offer_uri=https%3A%2F%2F127.0.0.1%3A9%2Foffer against a 127.0.0.1:9 TLS listener that only logs the ClientHello; MainActivity with a separate openid-credential-offer://?credential_offer= value that is a short dummy JSON offer containing no secret, token, or real credential; and OpenId4VpActivity with openid4vp://?request_uri=https%3A%2F%2F127.0.0.1%3A9%2Frequest against the same listener. Record whether a TCP connection or TLS ClientHello reaches 127.0.0.1:9 and whether provisioning leaves Idle. Do not complete issuance, approve a presentation, or install a local trust anchor. A failed handshake still counts as contact if the ClientHello is sent.
validation_plan.deployment: No production host or store signature is required. If the emulator result is inconclusive, read only the pinned Multipaz 0.100.0 sources for ProvisioningModel.launchOpenID4VCIProvisioning and UriSchemePresentmentActivity, and record whether each requests the supplied URI before consent and whether it rejects a private host or an inline credential_offer. Do not run those entry points against a real issuer, verifier, or credential.

title: Relay body readers retain the full request before authentication
description: readRawBody concatenates every chunk until the client ends the stream. createServer awaits it on POST /api/github-app/webhook before handleGithubAppWebhook checks GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET or the HMAC, and awaits readJsonBody, the same reader, on the other POST routes before origin or manage-key checks. Sibling copies readRaw (apps/pages/api/github-app/webhook.mjs, api.bodyParser false) and readBody (apps/pages/scripts/github-app-relay-plugin.mjs) repeat that missing ceiling instead of calling readRawBody. vercel.json sets no body limit. Outbound forge reads in pinned-fetch.mjs stop at 5 MiB; these inbound readers do not. A sandboxed call retained 1048576 bytes from readRawBody with no error. The Vercel handler retained a 1114112-byte stream (Buffer.concat length 1114112) and then returned 503 webhook_secret_unset; the same string on req.body also returned 503; GET returned 405 and did not read. The Vite git-backup route retained 1114112 bytes and then returned 403 origin_not_allowed, while an 8-byte truncated body was concatenated and returned 400 invalid_json. That plugin's webhook route also retained 1114112 bytes and then returned 500 because it passes the handler promise to writeRelayOutcome without awaiting it. Attacker cost is one upload. The process keeps the chunk list, the concatenated buffer, and the UTF-8 string, linear in the body, until the request ends or allocation fails. The raw body is not written to the webhook queue before authentication. The default relay listens on 127.0.0.1. The documented dev proxy listens on 0.0.0.0 and pipes /api/connect/* to this relay and other paths to Vite, still with no body ceiling.
root_cause: readRawBody appends every data chunk and concatenates them with no maximum, and createServer awaits that promise before authentication. readRaw and readBody are the same missing ceiling on the Vercel webhook adapter and the Vite dev relay.
intended_behavior: Each inbound reader should stop at one finite ceiling, destroy the socket, drop the chunk list, and fail the request with 413 before the bytes are kept and before secret, manage-key, or origin checks. Callers that catch every read error as invalid JSON or an empty body must preserve that 413. A ceiling added only in readRawBody does not cover the two copies.

trace.description: createServer accepts POST /api/github-app/webhook with no credential check before the body is read. Non-POST returns 405 first.
The route awaits readRawBody and only then parses JSON and calls handleGithubAppWebhook. A thrown read error is currently swallowed and the handler still runs.
Every data chunk is appended. Nothing compares the running size to a limit or destroys the request.
On end, Buffer.concat retains the whole body as one UTF-8 string. The webhook secret check in github-app-webhook.mjs runs only after this returns.

evidence.description: The data listener pushes each chunk into an array. readRawBody has no size constant or comparison.
Buffer.concat retains the whole body as one UTF-8 string. The local call produced concat length 1048576 and a resolved string of length 1048576, with no rejection.
readJsonBody is readRawBody plus JSON.parse, so every JSON route uses the same uncapped reader.
POST /api/github-app/webhook awaits readRawBody before handleGithubAppWebhook. The secret and HMAC checks are inside that later call.
Manage mutations await readJsonBody before handleManage, so the manage-key check runs only after the body is retained.
The process listens on HOST or 127.0.0.1 by default, so any local user can open the unauthenticated POST routes.
An unset GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET returns 503 webhook_secret_unset only after the caller has already built the body. The HMAC check is below this line.
api.bodyParser is false, so this Vercel route does not use a framework parser limit and reads the stream in readRaw.
readRaw pushes every streamed chunk and returns a pre-set string or Buffer with no byte-length check.
Buffer.concat retains the stream. The local POST produced concat length 1114112 and then 503 webhook_secret_unset. The same string on req.body also returned 503 without a further concat.
The handler awaits readRaw only after the POST check. GET returned 405 and did not start the body iterator.
The Vercel config sets install, build, output, headers, and rewrites only. It does not declare a function body size.
readBody appends every data chunk. It has no size constant and does not call readRawBody.
Buffer.concat retains the whole body before JSON.parse. The local git-backup POST produced concat length 1114112; the 8-byte truncated body was also concatenated before the parse error.
handleGitBackupRoute awaits readBody before handleGitBackupPut. The 1114112-byte body then got 403 origin_not_allowed; the truncated body got 400 invalid_json.
The origin refusal returns 403 origin_not_allowed on the already parsed object. It is not a body-size limit.
The Vite webhook branch awaits readBody before calling the webhook handler. That call concatenated 1114112 bytes.
writeRelayOutcome is given the handler promise without await, so after the retain the local webhook call returned 500 Cannot convert undefined or null to object rather than the secret check's status.
githubAppRelayPlugin is registered on the Vite dev server, so configureServer attaches readBody to that process.
dev:web runs vite on port 5180 with --host localhost. Other local users can open that loopback listener while the dev server is up.
Outbound forge responses are destroyed once they pass MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES (5 MiB). The inbound body readers do not share that control.
The dev proxy pipes the client request to the upstream with no body-length check.
Paths under /api/connect/ are forwarded to the relay, which reads them with readJsonBody. Every other path, including the Vite relay routes, is forwarded to the app port.
The proxy listens on 0.0.0.0, so when it is running a network client can reach the uncapped readers.

conditions.description: No credential is checked before the body is retained. The webhook secret and HMAC, the manage key, and the git-backup origin allowlist run only after the reader resolves. The local runs had GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET unset and no Origin.

The body is read by node server.mjs, the Vite dev middleware, or the Vercel adapter with api.bodyParser false. None of those readers, and not vercel.json, sets a byte ceiling. This result does not depend on an unverified platform edge limit.

The sender can open the listen socket. The default relay host is 127.0.0.1 and dev:web binds localhost, which other local users can open. Remote reachability requires a non-default HOST or the dev proxy listening on 0.0.0.0.

execution.attacker_perspective: A client that can reach the relay or the Vite dev server sends one large POST body before any secret, manage-key, or origin check.
payloads: four Buffer chunks of 262144 bytes each, emitted as data events to readRawBody
JSON {"pad":"a..."} totaling 1114112 bytes, as 64KiB stream chunks with req.body unset, and the same string assigned to req.body

the same 1114112-byte JSON body as 64KiB chunks POSTed to /api/git-backup/put with no Origin, an 8-byte truncated prefix {"pad":" on that route, and the 1114112-byte body POSTed to /api/github-app/webhook on the Vite middleware
instructions: Import readRawBody from apps/pages/server/manage.mjs, emit four 256KiB chunks and then end, and record whether the promise rejects and the resolved string length.

With GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET unset, call the default handler in apps/pages/api/github-app/webhook.mjs with the 1114112-byte JSON body streamed in 64KiB chunks, again with that string already on req.body, and once as GET with an iterator that throws if pulled.

Mount githubAppRelayPlugin().configureServer and invoke its middleware for POST /api/git-backup/put with the 1114112-byte body and no Origin, the same route with the 8-byte truncated body, and POST /api/github-app/webhook with the 1114112-byte body. Record status and Buffer.concat lengths.
execution.observed_result: readRawBody resolved with no error to a string of length 1048576 and Buffer.concat length 1048576. The streamed Vercel POST yielded concat length 1114112 and status 503 webhook_secret_unset. The string fast path also returned 503 webhook_secret_unset and did not concatenate. GET returned 405 and did not start the iterator. The Vite git-backup POST was concatenated to length 1114112 and returned 403 {"error":"origin_not_allowed"}. The 8-byte truncated body was concatenated and returned 400 {"error":"invalid_json"}. The Vite webhook route concatenated 1114112 bytes and then returned 500 Cannot convert undefined or null to object.

remediation.strategy: Cap readRawBody, readRaw, and readBody at one shared finite ceiling, on the order of the relay's existing 5 MiB outbound cap and large enough for one legitimate sealed backup. When the running size crosses it, drop the chunk list, destroy the socket, and reject with a 413 before JSON.parse and before secret, manage-key, or origin checks. In createServer, map that error to HTTP 413 on the webhook branch, which today swallows every read error and still calls the handler, and on every readJsonBody catch, which today turns every failure into 400 invalid_json. In the Vercel handler, return 413 before handleGithubAppWebhook. In the Vite plugin, do not map 413 to invalid_json, and do not ignore a read failure on the webhook branch. A cap only in manage.mjs leaves the two copies exposed.

likelihood.reason: The readers are unauthenticated, but the default relay binds 127.0.0.1 and dev:web binds localhost. Another local user can open those ports. A remote client reaches them only when HOST is changed or the optional dev proxy is listening on 0.0.0.0. The public Vercel route is the readRaw copy; this rating does not assume an absent platform edge limit.

impact.reason: The demonstrated cost is memory linear in one request body, as the chunk list, concatenated buffer, and UTF-8 string, inside the one relay or dev-server process until the request ends or allocation fails. The raw body is not queued and vault data is not disclosed. If allocation kills the process, the relay script has no supervisor and stays down until restarted.

confidence.reason: None of the three readers compares accumulated size to a ceiling, and their callers await them before the secret, manage-key, or origin checks. A sandboxed local run retained 1048576 bytes from readRawBody and 1114112 bytes from readRaw and readBody before those later responses.

title: Default /tmp webhook queue symlink follow does not cross users
description: Off Vercel, with CONNECT_WEBHOOK_QUEUE_PATH and the Redis REST variables unset, enqueueWebhookNudge stores nudges at /tmp/opensesame-github-webhook-queue.json using readFileSync and writeFileSync, which do not pass O_NOFOLLOW. A symlink owned by the relay uid is followed, so a valid webhook HMAC replaces the target with queue JSON. The claimed attacker is a different local user planting that name in sticky /tmp. This host's fs.protected_symlinks and fs.protected_regular policy is the control for that directory, and the executed write never left the relay uid. crates/sealed-store/src/path.rs writes with O_NOFOLLOW; this queue does not share that pattern. That difference is calibration only and does not show another user crossing /tmp.
claimed_root_cause: writeFileQueue and readFileQueue open the predictable /tmp queue path with filesystem calls that follow a final symlink and never check that the opened inode is a regular file created by the relay, so another local user can redirect an authorized write onto a file the relay can replace.

trace.description: POST /api/github-app/webhook passes the parsed body, request headers, and raw body to handleGithubAppWebhook.
After verifyGithubWebhookSignature returns null, the handler enqueues a nudge with the delivery id, installation id, and receivedAt.
When Redis and VERCEL are unset, enqueueWebhookNudge appends through readFileQueue and writeFileQueue. drainWebhookNudges calls that same writer at line 179.
writeFileSync writes the queue JSON to queuePath() with no open flags and no inode check, so it does not request O_NOFOLLOW.

title: Tenant join grants organization membership to the caller after verified-email auto-link binds the identity to another principal
description: POST /v1/organizations/tenants/:slug/join authenticates the caller with any live provisional bearer, verifies the organization id_token, and asks attachVerifiedExternalIdentity to bind the subject. When the token carries an email the organization is allowed to treat as verified and another principal already owns that verified email, the new identity row is stored on that other principal. The join handler then calls jitJoinOrganization with the caller's principal id. The caller receives the membership, including owner when an active SCIM row maps the subject to owner, while the identity remains on the email owner. The caller's session is left on the original provisional principal.

Verified-email auto-link (ADR 0057 D15) can make those two ids differ. organizationMemberships.upsert then records the caller, and provisionedRoleForSubject supplies the role from the IdP subject rather than from the principal that owns the identity.
intended_behavior: The membership principal is the principal that owns the verified identity. attachVerifiedExternalIdentity documents that callers must follow the returned identity.principalId. When that id differs from the caller, the caller is not an organization member and is not given a 201 join response. Hosted SSO, LDAP, and SAML already pass the linked principal into jitJoinOrganization. An id_token whose subject tuple is already owned by someone else continues to return 409 before any membership write.

The route verifies the posted id_token for the organization SSO or SAML issuer with origin audiences and a 600 second maximum age before any membership is written.
The verified subject is attached with emailLinkFields for trust source org. A DNS-verified organization domain lets the email act as an account join key.

The new verified identity is stored with principalId ownerPrincipalId and returned on the success result. A tuple already owned by another principal returns identity_collision instead.
The handler still passes the caller principalId into jitJoinOrganization and uses provisionedRoleForSubject(org, assertion.sub) for the role.

title: SCIM deprovision does not revoke members who signed in through the organization LDAP directory
description: PATCH or DELETE that deactivates a SCIM user is supposed to drop that subject's membership and the provisional sessions that membership authorized. principalsForSubject searches kinds oidc, oauth2, saml, ldap, and email, but only under organization.ssoIssuer and organization.samlIssuer. LDAP sign-in stores the external identity as kind ldap with issuer ldapIssuer(config), the directory URL's scheme, host, and port, which is not either of those strings. The handler still returns 200 after deprovision and does not check that anyone was revoked. revokeOrganizationMembership, the only revocation on this path, is therefore not called, so the membership row and provisional sessions stay. The same call does revoke a principal whose oidc identity is stored under ssoIssuer. applyRole uses the same lookup, so a Groups role push misses these members too. When native SAML is configured with metadata and samlIssuer is empty, admission stores the metadata entityID, and that issuer is also absent from this list. Directory sync does not close the gap: it revokes an LDAP member only when a later scan no longer contains that subject.

intended_behavior: Deactivating or deleting a SCIM user revokes membership and live provisional sessions for every principal of this organization whose external identity subject is that user's externalId, userName, or a remembered previous subject, including principals admitted by this organization's LDAP directory.

After the SCIM row is saved inactive, deprovision is the only revocation. The handler then audits success and returns 200 whether or not any principal was found.
Issuers are only organization.ssoIssuer and organization.samlIssuer. kind ldap is queried, but with those issuers, not ldapIssuer of the org LDAP config.
revokeOrganizationMembership runs only for principals returned by that lookup. The LDAP principal is not among them, so the membership row and provisional sessions stay.

A found principal is revoked only when it has a membership in this organization. That check is never reached for an identity stored under the directory issuer.
applyRole resolves principals through the same principalsForUser lookup, so a Groups role push misses the same directory identities.
ldapIssuer returns protocol plus host of the directory URL, dropping path and query, for example ldaps://dir.acme.example:636.
attachVerifiedExternalIdentity persists kind ldap and that ldapIssuer value as the identity used on later sign-in.
Membership removal happens only inside revokeOrganizationMembership, which deprovision does not call when the lookup misses.
The same helper deletes provisional sessions for that principal only after the membership row was removed.
The PATCH responds 200 with the inactive user after deprovision returns, with no check that a membership was removed.
If samlIssuer is empty, SAML admission stores the metadata entityID instead, which this issuer list also does not search. A non-empty samlIssuer is stored and is searched.

title: Invocation policy admits IPv4-mapped loopback and private request URIs
description: validate_platform_invocation is documented to reject private or loopback request URIs before it builds the protocol URI handed to the wallet. host_is_private applies std's IPv4 special-range helpers and a few IPv6 flags, but never unwraps an IPv4-mapped address. url 2.5.8 keeps a bracketed IPv4-mapped literal as Host::Ipv6 and serializes https://[::ffff:127.0.0.1]/request as https://[::ffff:7f00:1]/request, which the same function rejects when written as dotted 127.0.0.1. Executing that parser together with host_is_private's match accepted the mapped forms of 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254, 10.1.2.3, and 192.168.0.1 and would copy them into protocol_uri. MainActivity's https branch forwards that protocol URI into OpenId4VpActivity or launchOpenID4VCIProvisioning. Any sender that can deliver a VIEW intent can put the configured invocation host in the URI string; the origin check does not identify the caller. As calibration only, connector-host::is_blocked_v6 and connection-broker::is_internal already apply the embedded IPv4 checks to mapped addresses; authenticator-core does not.
root_cause: host_is_private classifies IPv6 only with is_loopback, is_unspecified, is_unique_local, is_unicast_link_local, and is_multicast. IPv4-mapped addresses in ::ffff:0:0/96 fail those flags, and the function never applies the IPv4 checks to IpAddr::to_ipv4_mapped.
intended_behavior: A request_uri whose host is loopback, link-local, or RFC1918 must be rejected as PrivateRequestUri whether it is written as a dotted IPv4 literal or as an IPv4-mapped IPv6 literal, and no protocol URI containing that host may be returned.

trace.description: MainActivity is exported with no permission and handles VIEW data. Another app can set an explicit intent whose URI string uses the configured invocation origin; the intent-filter host does not authenticate the caller.
https URIs are admitted solely by the Result of validatePlatformInvocation; a successful return is treated as a safe protocol request.
The IPv6 arm does not unwrap IPv4-mapped addresses, so ::ffff:7f00:1 (127.0.0.1), ::ffff:a9fe:a9fe (169.254.169.254), and mapped RFC1918 hosts are not private.
The accepted protocol_uri, including the mapped request host, is parsed and set as the VIEW data for OpenId4VpActivity. The oid4vci branch passes the same string to launchOpenID4VCIProvisioning.

evidence.description: Private request URIs are rejected only when host_is_private is true. allow_private_request_uris is false for InvocationPolicy::new, which is what validate_platform_invocation uses.
IPv6 classification omits to_ipv4_mapped. Bracketed IPv4-mapped hosts stay IPv6, so ::ffff:7f00:1 misses every flag in this match while dotted 127.0.0.1 is rejected.
On success the normalized request URL is copied into payload, and the following match builds an openid4vp or openid-credential-offer protocol URI from that string.
OID4VP success starts OpenId4VpActivity with setData(Uri.parse(invocation.protocolUri)). There is no second private-host check.
OID4VCI success passes invocation.protocolUri to launchOpenID4VCIProvisioning.

conditions.description: No authenticator-origin credential is required. The sender only has to place the configured https origin in the invocation URI string.
MainActivity is exported and its https branch forwards accepted protocol URIs. The default invocation host is a DNS name baked into https://${INVOCATION_HOST}.

execution.attacker_perspective: Another app on the device, or any component that can deliver a VIEW intent to the exported wallet activity, supplies an otherwise well-formed invocation whose request_uri host is the IPv4-mapped form of a loopback, link-local, or RFC1918 address.
instructions: Build the opensesame-authenticator-core rlib from crates/authenticator-core at this commit with the default features.
Call validate_platform_invocation with origin https://auth.opensesame.example and each payload.
For each accepted IPv6 host, call Ipv6Addr::to_ipv4_mapped.
execution.observed_result: Dotted https://127.0.0.1/request and https://[::1]/request were private and rejected. https://[::ffff:127.0.0.1]/request was not: url 2.5.8 parses the bracketed literal as IPv6 and serializes it as payload https://[::ffff:7f00:1]/request with protocol_uri openid4vp://?request_uri=https%3A%2F%2F%5B%3A%3Affff%3A7f00%3A1%5D%2Frequest, and to_ipv4_mapped was 127.0.0.1. Mapped 169.254.169.254 was accepted as an Oid4vci credential_offer_uri https://[::ffff:a9fe:a9fe]/latest. Mapped 10.1.2.3 and 192.168.0.1 were accepted as Oid4vp payloads https://[::ffff:a01:203]/x and https://[::ffff:c0a8:1]/x. Dotted 169.254.169.254 was rejected. host_is_private's IPv6 arm does not call to_ipv4_mapped, and validate_platform_invocation copies the normalized URL into protocol_uri with no further host check.
