For IPv6, if to_ipv4_mapped() is Some, apply the same IPv4 private, loopback, link-local, multicast, broadcast, and unspecified checks. Add a regression that the four accepted mapped payloads above return PrivateRequestUri while a public https request URI still succeeds.

likelihood.reason: MainActivity is exported with no permission. A second local app can deliver one explicit VIEW intent whose URI string uses the configured origin. No credential or user gesture is required for the policy function to accept the mapped host.

impact.reason: A loopback, link-local metadata, or RFC1918 URL is labeled safe and placed in the protocol URI that the https handler forwards into presentment or provisioning. That is the admission boundary the private-URI check exists to enforce. This run did not observe a socket or a credential disclosure, so the impact is not device compromise.

confidence.reason: host_is_private's IPv6 match and url 2.5.8's IPv6 parser and serializer were executed together. They rejected dotted 127.0.0.1 and [::1], accepted the mapped equivalents, and std::net::Ipv6Addr::to_ipv4_mapped identified the embedded addresses. MainActivity forwards protocolUri with no second private-host check.

title: Publishing a breach occurrence count is the documented event boundary
description: A positive POST /api/v1/security/breach-check does publish breach.password.compromised with the Pwned Passwords occurrence count joined to the caller-supplied subject, and default logs plus configured sinks keep that integer. That copy is the contract, not a crossed boundary. The BreachEvent module comment says the corpus count is a property of the corpus, not of the secret, and is published because it makes a finding actionable. The value-blind payload test requires the number to remain while secret-shaped keys stay absent. No smaller public-corpus preimage of any count was shown, so the integer was not shown to name a plaintext.
claimed_root_cause: BreachEvent::password_compromised stores the corpus frequency as ordinary metadata and the notice path copies it, still bound to the subject, into the default log and every matching sink. No scrub or renderer buckets or removes that integer, which the candidate treats as a disagreement with the value-blind rule if the public corpus maps the count to a small set of plaintexts.

trace.description: After authorize has required an owner, admin, or operator, line 244 sets occurrences from password_occurrences of the digest of the caller-supplied candidate. That helper returns only the local suffix-match count. The caller already holds the candidate and is not a lower-trust principal.

A non-zero count builds BreachEvent::password_compromised for the caller-supplied subject. The same integer is stored on the finding and returned to that caller. event.notice is published only when the finding row newly opens.
The password-compromised summary names the subject and interpolates the exact occurrence count. payload inserts that same integer as the JSON number occurrences beside subject metadata.

publish forwards notice.scrubbed to the notifier, alerter, task bus, and delivery ledger. Scrubbing drops secret-shaped keys and secret-pattern strings and leaves the corpus count for those designed security-event readers.

evidence.description: The module contract says the one corpus number, how many times a password appears, is a property of the corpus rather than of the secret, and is what makes a finding actionable. That is why it is published.
The occurrences field comment states it is a property of the corpus and says nothing about the secret's content.
payload_is_value_blind asserts that occurrences remains in the payload while secret-shaped keys are forbidden. The value-blind rule includes this integer.
The firing-sink test keeps custom_details.occurrences and asserts a password key and its plaintext do not reach the body. Keeping the count is the checked boundary.

The ledger refuses a hash or hash prefix because a stored SHA-1 is a crackable artifact. The count is not given that treatment, and a match is still published as breach.password.compromised against the named subject.
The breach-check route comment says a positive result is published so the same subscribers, notifier, and alerting see it, rather than leaving the answer only in the HTTP response.

The authorized caller who submitted the candidate receives the same occurrence count in the JSON response. Host logs and configured sinks are the additional readers that route and ADR 0080 already name.

reason: Source shows that publishing the occurrence count is the intended boundary, and no smaller preimage was shown. The module comment at crates/breach-intel/src/event.rs lines 8-10 and the field comment at lines 66-67 define the count as corpus metadata that says nothing about the secret and is published because it makes the finding actionable. The value-blind unit test and the PagerDuty renderer test both require that integer to survive while secret material is removed. ADR 0080 treats a stored SHA-1, not this count, as the crackable copy the product refuses to keep, and it still publishes breach.password.compromised to the security-event feed. The check is limited to an owner, admin, or operator, who is also returned the count. redact_json cloning non-strings matches that contract. The outbound range request still sends only a five-hex prefix. The candidate itself records that the public corpus was not loaded and that plaintext recovery was not shown, so the count was not established as an identifier of the secret.

title: Sandbox broker calls ignore grant expiry after the profile is minted
description: SandboxProfile::from_grant_chain stores the chain's earliest expires_at and clamps ResourceBudget.deadline to the remainder at that instant, and never above the 5 second platform ceiling. Sandbox::spawn then accepts untrusted guest bytes after only RevocationFence::check, once before compile and again before the guest entry. fresh_store arms Store::set_epoch_deadline with deadline_ticks of that stored Duration. Wasmtime 36.0.17 (Cargo.lock) implements set_epoch_deadline as current engine epoch plus the delta (store.rs StoreInner::set_epoch_deadline), so the interval is rebased to fresh_store rather than cut off at expires_at. still_authorized, used by emit, http-fetch, sign, and token-acquire, returns fence.check and does not read profile.expires_at or the clock. The expires_at getter has no caller in this crate, and binds_chain does not compare the window. Source therefore links whatever broker imports the profile granted and reaches Broker after only a live fence, including when Utc::now() is already past expires_at, and a spawn that starts with time left can still run until mint-time deadline after expires_at by the delay before fresh_store (compile happens first) or by any later spawn on the same Sandbox. Each spawn gets a fresh interval of at most that mint-time deadline, not an unbounded single run. No workspace crate calls Sandbox::spawn. Gateway finish_dispatch does re-check grant.assert_active(Utc::now()) immediately before its broker side effect; connector-host rebases an epoch deadline the same way but does not carry this grant window. The post-expiry broker invocation itself was not executed.
claimed_root_cause: Authority lifetime is enforced only as a Duration clamp inside from_grant_chain. Spawn, fresh_store, and still_authorized treat a live RevocationFence as sufficient authorization and re-base the epoch deadline on the engine epoch at fresh_store instead of the absolute expires_at.

trace.description: Untrusted guest bytes enter spawn. The only authorization check here, and the only one repeated at line 163 before the guest runs, is fence.check. Nothing compares Utc::now() with profile.expires_at, so a profile minted inside the window still passes after the window has closed while the generation fence is live.

set_epoch_deadline is given deadline_ticks of the mint-time Duration. That value is not recomputed from profile.expires_at, and wasmtime adds it to the engine's current epoch, so the wall-clock budget starts at fresh_store.
The call-time gate returns fence.check and does not read the cloned profile's expires_at or the clock. GuestState carries the profile, but the shims use it for byte caps only.

After still_authorized, the guest destination is passed to Broker::http_fetch. sign_impl (Broker::sign), token_impl (Broker::token_acquire), and emit_impl (Broker::emit) use the same fence-only check. RunContext carries organization and grant ids, not expires_at.

evidence.description: from_grant_chain takes the earliest grant expires_at, converts expires_at minus now into a Duration, clamps the budget with that remainder, and stores the timestamp. The DateTime is not read again except by its getter.
expires_at() is the only read of the stored timestamp. No other file in the repository calls SandboxProfile::expires_at.
binds_chain compares leaf id, root id, organization id, and invalidation generation only. It does not test the validity window.
ResourceBudget::CEILING.deadline is Duration::from_secs(5), so the mint-time clamp is at most five seconds.
clamped_to_remaining documents that a run may not outlive the grant, but the body only mins deadline with the Duration the caller already computed at profile construction.
deadline_ticks converts a Duration to epoch ticks rounded up, with a floor of one tick. It has no absolute timestamp.
RevocationFence::is_live is the kill flag and ledger generation equality. Time passing does not move the ledger, so an unrevoked fence stays live after expires_at. check() only calls is_live.
a_stale_profile_cannot_start_a_run_at_all expects spawn to return Revoked after a generation bump. No sandbox test sleeps past expires_at and expects spawn or a broker call to fail.
The same Sandbox value is spawned twice. The public API is built for reuse, so a retained engine is the normal shape, not a one-shot that ends at mint.

Calibration only: finish_dispatch reauthorize calls grant.assert_active(Utc::now()) immediately before the broker side effect. The sandbox path has no equivalent call. This does not dismiss the sandbox gap.

blockers: Spawn after expires_at was not executed. sandbox-run.sh with RUSTUP_HOME=/usr/local/rustup and CARGO_HOME=/usr/local/cargo can run rustc 1.88.0, but cargo test -p opensesame-sandbox --offline --locked --manifest-path /workspace/Cargo.toml --features wasm-runtime,fixtures --no-run is killed with signal 25 (SIGXFSZ) while compiling syn, before opensesame-sandbox or wasmtime is built. ulimit -f is 10240 (about 5 MiB), ulimit -v is 1048576 KiB, ulimit -t is 25, and the wrapper timeout is 25s. /workspace/target does not exist and no libwasmtime or libopensesame_sandbox rlib is on disk. Source control flow is unambiguous that the broker call is not gated on expires_at; the missing fact is the observed spawn result against a recording broker.

validation_plan.local: On a normal toolchain, offline and locked, with a writable target directory outside the audit sandbox: cargo test -p opensesame-sandbox --offline --locked --features wasm-runtime,fixtures. Use a chain whose ttl is a few seconds and whose actions include sandbox.http, mint the profile, keep the revocation fence live, and sleep until Utc::now() is past profile.expires_at(). Spawn a one-call http-fetch module on the in-crate RecordingBroker (no network, no live credential) and record whether spawn returns Ok and whether fetched() contains the guest destination. Separately, spawn while less than the mint-time deadline remains and record whether that broker call is entered after expires_at. Do not revoke the fence and do not point the broker at a real host.
validation_plan.deployment: No deployed service is required. No workspace crate calls Sandbox::spawn. The owner check is the same local cargo test. If an integrator already holds a Sandbox across a grant window, observe only whether their Broker::http_fetch is entered after expires_at with the fence still live, using a recording double rather than a production credential or network fetch.

title: Daemon loopback proxy canonicalizes backslash paths into the blocked local session mint
description: The daemon router mounts /host/{*path} and /identity/{*path} with any() and no operator gate. proxy_loopback allows only a loopback base, then denies a slash-split rest that percent-decodes to exactly api, v1, session, local, and denies a segment that percent-decodes to a single dot or a double dot. It concatenates that raw rest onto the host base and reqwest 0.12.28 parses the string with url 2.5.8. On an http URL that parser treats a raw backslash as a separator and removes dot segments, so /api/v1/session/.\local, /api/v1/foo/..\session/local, and /api/v1/session/.\.\local miss both denials while Url::parse yields /api/v1/session/local. Redirects are disabled, so that normalized path is the upstream request-target. The proxy drops X-OpenSesame-Operator and hop or forwarding headers and still copies Authorization. Host token_from_headers accepts Authorization: Bearer operator:<token> or the bearer-lowercase form when Origin is absent. local_mint requires that operator token, returns 403 local_session_forbidden when the host has production_safeguards, and otherwise requires demo bootstrap before its success response sets access_token to opaque-session:<id> for 300 seconds with the demo principal as owner. The local test stopped at URL and HTTP/1 parsing and did not mint a session. Same-machine loopback is not this boundary: the product treats loopback as same-machine authority, and that caller can open the host port. The source-visible off-loopback path is OPENSESAME_DAEMON_NETWORK_BRIDGE=1 binding this same router on the WSL eth address. windows_loopback_reaches_daemon is true only when Windows curl stdout contains opensesame-daemon; GET /health is {"status":"ok"}, so a successful loopback fetch does not suppress that bind. tailscale serve --bg also publishes the listener; preservation of a raw backslash through that proxy was not executed. Percent-encoded %5C and %2F stay in one segment and do not parse as /api/v1/session/local.
root_cause: The proxy denylist and dot-segment check split the raw request-target on '/' and percent-decode each segment once. The outbound http URL parser applies WHATWG special-scheme rules, which turn a raw '\' into '/' and then collapse '.' and '..'. The checks never see the path that is requested.
intended_behavior: A request that the outbound URL parser will turn into /api/v1/session/local must be rejected at the proxy, including raw backslash and dot-segment forms. Other /host routes may still carry Authorization so a tailnet client can call the loopback host. The whois tailnet listener stays limited to health, discovery, and slot-key device routes.

trace.description: router mounts /host/{*path} with any(proxy_host) and no require_operator layer. The same function also mounts /host, /identity, and /identity/{*path}. secured_router wraps this router and is the app the network bridge serves.
When OPENSESAME_DAEMON_NETWORK_BRIDGE is exactly 1, run calls spawn_wsl_bridge with that app and startup::enable_network_bridge. This block is not the whois listener.

If wsl_bridge_listen returns an address other than the primary listen, the daemon binds it and axum-serves the same app. That helper returns the WSL eth address when the process is WSL, the resolved tailscale binary is the Windows executable, and hostname -I yields a non-loopback IPv4, unless windows_loopback_reaches_daemon is true. That probe requires curl stdout to contain opensesame-daemon. GET /health returns {"status":"ok"}, so a successful loopback health fetch does not suppress the eth bind.

After base_url_is_local, the /host prefix returns 403 only when is_local_session_path(rest) is true, then 400 when has_dot_segment(rest) is true. Both helpers see req.uri().path(), which httparse 1.10.1 and http 1.5.0 keep when it contains a raw backslash. hyper 1.11.0 builds that URI from those two parsers and was not executed itself.

has_dot_segment and is_local_session_path split only on '/' and compare one-pass percent-decoded segments. A raw backslash stays inside a segment, so '.\local' and '..\session' match neither the local-session tuple nor '.' or '..'.

The outbound URL is the base trimmed of trailing slashes, plus the raw rest, plus the raw query. Client::request parses that string with url 2.5.8. The client was built with redirect Policy::none, so the parsed URL is the request that is sent.
Forwarding skips hop and forwarding headers and the header name x-opensesame-operator. Authorization is copied, including Bearer operator:<token>. The proxy does not add the daemon operator token.
When Origin is absent, the host operator check accepts Authorization Bearer operator: or bearer operator:. The stripped X-OpenSesame-Operator form is not required.

The success JSON of POST /api/v1/session/local sets access_token to opaque-session:<id> with expires_in 300. The handler reaches this only after require_operator, a production_safeguards 403, and require_demo_bootstrap, and it stores an owner local session for the demo principal. The route is mounted from local_authority_routes. The local test did not call this handler.

evidence.description: proxy_never_forwards_local_session_mint expects 403 for the exact path, a double slash, and %73ession. It does not include a raw backslash.
is_local_session_path requires the decoded non-empty segments to be exactly api, v1, session, local. A failed percent-decode makes the predicate false, so a bad encoding does not deny.

The workspace pins url 2.5.8. Its special-scheme parser rewrites a raw backslash to '/' and shortens '.' and '..' segments. The sandbox parse of the three backslash rests returned /api/v1/session/local.
The workspace pins reqwest 0.12.28. Client::request for &str calls Url::parse.
The daemon reqwest client is built with redirect Policy::none, so a parsed URL is not followed to a second location.
The workspace pins http 1.5.0. Its path class 0x40..=0x5F includes byte 0x5C, and the sandbox Uri::try_from kept /host/api/v1/session/.\local.
The workspace pins httparse 1.10.1. The sandbox parsed POST /host/api/v1/session/.\local HTTP/1.1 and httparse returned that path with the backslash.

The workspace pins matchit 0.8.4. Its catch-all consumes the remaining path bytes and splits static segments only on '/'. A sandbox Router with /host and /host/{*path} matched /host/api/v1/session/.\local, /host/api/v1/foo/..\session/local, and /host/api/v1/session/.\.\local to the catch-all and captured each raw rest, including the backslash.

network_bridge_enabled replaces daemon exposure with Networked before from_env, so production_safeguards is true for the daemon process only. A separate local-only development host is unchanged, and a loopback http host_api still passes the daemon upstream check.

enable_serve runs tailscale serve --bg against serve_target. On WSL with Windows tailscale.exe, serve_target is the non-loopback eth URL unless windows_loopback_reaches_daemon is true, and otherwise http://127.0.0.1:<port>. The probe looks for opensesame-daemon in curl stdout, which GET /health does not return. Preservation of a raw backslash through that proxy is not in this repository and was not executed.
The optional tailscale-feature listener routes only GET /health, POST /v1/discover, and vault device routes behind whois_gate. It does not mount /host or /identity. Empty allowlists do not bind.

When a Tailscale Serve HTTPS URL is known, pairing_view advertises host_api as {url}/host and identity_api as {url}/identity. Publishing those prefixes is intentional. The defect is the session-mint denylist, not the publish itself.
local_authority_routes mounts POST /api/v1/session/local on session::local_mint.
require_demo_bootstrap returns 503 demo_bootstrap_unavailable when no bootstrap state is stored.
maybe_demo_bootstrap seeds the demo principal only when OPENSESAME_DEV_BOOTSTRAP is true or 1 and the host deployment does not have production_safeguards.
Sync push calls require_session and does not accept the operator token. The session the denylist withholds is what this route requires.
session_scope calls require_session only. Listing or creating connections in the session organization needs the opaque session, not the raw operator bearer.
production_safeguards is true for Production mode or Networked exposure. A host that stays LocalOnly development does not set it, so local_mint stays available on that process.
base_url_is_local accepts only an http or https base whose host is loopback and which has no userinfo. The proxy is not a general SSRF; the bypass is the one denylisted path on that loopback base.

conditions.description: The caller can deliver an HTTP/1 request-target containing a raw backslash to the daemon listener and cannot open the host loopback port. Same-machine loopback is outside this boundary because that caller can POST the host directly. The in-repo off-loopback bind is the WSL eth listener under the bridge flag. tailscale serve --bg also publishes the listener; preservation of '\' through the Tailscale proxy was not executed.

OPENSESAME_DAEMON_NETWORK_BRIDGE must be exactly 1. The direct off-loopback bind also requires WSL, a resolved Windows tailscale.exe, and a non-loopback IPv4 from hostname -I. windows_loopback_reaches_daemon does not treat a successful curl of http://127.0.0.1:<port>/health as reachability, because the body is {"status":"ok"} and the probe requires the substring opensesame-daemon. The host process must be development or test and LocalOnly. OPENSESAME_DEV_BOOTSTRAP must be true or 1. The daemon bridge does not flip the host process to Networked.

The caller presents Authorization: Bearer operator:<the host operator token> or the bearer-lowercase form, and does not send Origin. X-OpenSesame-Operator is stripped by the proxy and does not authorize the mint. Without this bearer, local_mint returns 401.

The host API base must pass base_url_is_local, which http://127.0.0.1:8787 does. If host production_safeguards is on, the forwarded mint returns 403 local_session_forbidden and no session is issued. If demo bootstrap was not seeded, the result is 503.

Outbound parsing is url 2.5.8 via reqwest 0.12.28, and inbound parsing is httparse 1.10.1 plus http 1.5.0, as pinned in Cargo.lock. Those are the versions the sandbox checks ran. Routing uses matchit 0.8.4, which was executed: the three /host backslash request-targets selected the catch-all.

execution.attacker_perspective: A network client of the daemon HTTP listener who already holds the host operator token in bearer form, and who cannot connect to the host port, sends the local-session path with a raw backslash under the /host prefix.
instructions: Copy decoded_path_segment, has_dot_segment, and is_local_session_path verbatim from crates/daemon/src/proxy_path.rs and parse http://127.0.0.1:8787 plus each rest with url 2.5.8.
Compare the exact local-session path, a slash .. form, a %2e form, the three backslash rests with the /host prefix removed, and the %5C and %2F negative controls.
Parse the HTTP/1 request POST /host/api/v1/session/.\local HTTP/1.1 with Host: 127.0.0.1:18790 using httparse 1.10.1 and http 1.5.0, and print Uri::path.
Do not start the daemon or the host. Stop after the parser result. Do not mint a session.
Insert /host and /host/{*path} into matchit 0.8.4 and match the three /host backslash request-targets. Do not start the daemon or the host and do not mint a session.
execution.observed_result: url 2.5.8 and the copied predicates printed: exact rest session_deny=true dot_deny=false parsed path=/api/v1/session/local; slash .. and %2e forms dot_deny=true and the same parsed path; /api/v1/session/.\local, /api/v1/foo/..\session/local, and /api/v1/session/.\.\local all printed session_deny=false dot_deny=false and parsed path=/api/v1/session/local. %5Clocal and %2Flocal printed session_deny=false dot_deny=false and stayed on /api/v1/session/%5Clocal and /api/v1/session/%2Flocal. httparse 1.10.1 completed and returned the path containing one backslash; http 1.5.0 Uri::path kept /host/api/v1/session/.\local. matchit 0.8.4 selected the /host/{*path} catch-all for /host/api/v1/session/.\local, /host/api/v1/foo/..\session/local, and /host/api/v1/session/.\.\local and captured each raw rest with the backslash. No opaque-session token was minted.

remediation.strategy: Decide the denylist on the path reqwest will request. Keep the slash-segment dot check, parse the outbound URL, and apply is_local_session_path to the parsed path so every normalization to /api/v1/session/local, including a raw backslash collapse, is 403. Reject any other raw backslash in the rest with 400. Add the three backslash payloads next to proxy_never_forwards_local_session_mint. Do not strip Authorization globally; other /host routes are meant to carry the operator bearer. Leave the whois listener unchanged.

likelihood.reason: The caller must already hold the host operator token, the host must be non-production and local-only with demo bootstrap on, and the request must reach a daemon listener the caller can use while the host port stays closed. The bridge flag, WSL, and a Windows tailscale.exe are explicit opt-ins. A successful Windows curl of /health does not suppress the eth bind, because that probe requires the substring opensesame-daemon and the health body is {"status":"ok"}. Loopback on the same machine does not need this bypass, and Tailscale Serve's handling of backslash was not shown.

impact.reason: Source of local_mint shows a 300-second owner opaque-session for the demo principal only. Sync push and credential-connection routes accept that session and reject the raw operator token. Host production safeguards still return 403. The local test did not issue a token, and the session is not an arbitrary tenant.

confidence.reason: The guard miss and the url 2.5.8 rewrite were executed again in the sandbox: the three raw-backslash rests had session_deny=false, dot_deny=false, and parsed path /api/v1/session/local, while %5C and %2F stayed encoded. httparse 1.10.1 and http 1.5.0 kept the backslash, and matchit 0.8.4 routed those request-targets to the /host catch-all. Header forwarding, redirect Policy::none, host bearer acceptance, and the demo-bootstrap gate are direct source with no later re-check of the canonical path. The live mint, hyper, and Tailscale Serve were not run.

title: Path-scoped egress allowlist accepts encoded traversals that decode outside the prefix
description: EgressBinding::allows_url is the destination fence on the connection-owner level-2 invoke path before the sealed bearer is attached. New connections default to max_invoke_level 2. Delegates are refused above level 1. The owner grant minted from the catalog lists the provider's operations, and invoke_network_json checks only that the operation name is in that list. The later OpenFGA check, when configured, also sees subject, operation, and resource, not the URL. After url 2.5.8 WHATWG parsing, a non-empty path_prefixes entry matches when Url::path() equals the prefix or starts with that prefix plus a slash. A whole segment that is exactly .. or %2e%2e is collapsed, so https://api.doppler.com/v3/projects/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/configs/config/secrets becomes /configs/config/secrets and fails the prefix test, and the literal values path /v3/configs/config/secrets fails it too. A traversal glued to %2f, a semicolon, or %5c is not a whole dot segment. Applied to Doppler prefixes [/v3/projects, /v3/configs/config/secrets/names], Cloudflare Origin CA [/client/v4/certificates], a custom base path such as /api/v2, and OpenRouter [/api/v1/], those forms stay under the prefix and pass. url.as_str() keeps the encoded target, and reqwest 0.12.28 builds the HTTP URI from that string on http_bytes, which uses redirect Policy::none. One percent-decode of the accepted Doppler target /v3/projects/%2e%2e%2fconfigs/config/secrets is /v3/projects/../configs/config/secrets, which resolves to the values path the catalog test says must stay unreachable. The in-repo surrogate check_scope refuses dot segments, backslash, and semicolon on both the raw path and one percent-decode because upstream resolution is not predictable. allows_url does not. Whether Doppler, Cloudflare, OpenRouter, or a custom origin performs that decode is not in this repository.
claimed_root_cause: allows_url decides path scope from Url::path() with a segment-boundary prefix test and never percent-decodes the path or rejects .., backslash, or semicolon segments. authorized_json treats that Ok as sufficient and http_authorized attaches the sealed credential to the original URL.

trace.description: When invoke_level is 2 and the resolved connection is broker-backed, the caller JSON parameters.url is copied into ConstrainedHttpInput with no path normalization.
Level-2 authorization accepts the URL when this same allows_url returns Ok. It does not decode the path or bind the operation to a path.
The copied URL is passed to invoke_network_json together with the caller operation name.
The operation is accepted when its name is in the provider list. The URL is not compared to that operation.
After the row is in-org and Active, the only destination check is row.egress.allows_url(url). Ok continues into credential opening.
A non-empty path_prefixes list allows the WHATWG path when it equals a prefix or starts with that prefix plus a slash, including segments such as %2e%2e%2fconfigs, ..%2f..%2f, ..;, and %5c..%5c.
credential_header's sealed access token is set on the request for the caller URL. The http_bytes client does not follow redirects.

evidence.description: The compared path is Url::path(), which leaves %2f, %5c, and semicolon inside a segment.
Path scope is path == prefix or path.starts_with(prefix + '/'), using the WHATWG path only. There is no second decode.
authorized_json returns before opening the credential only when allows_url fails. An Ok continues into credential injection.
http_authorized sends the caller URL on self.http_bytes, the client built with redirect Policy::none.
credential_header's value is set on the outbound request for the caller URL.
http_bytes is built with reqwest redirect Policy::none, so a 3xx is not followed with the bearer.
DEFAULT_MAX_INVOKE_LEVEL is 2, so a new connection's ceiling includes constrained HTTP unless an owner lowers it.
A delegate is refused when invoke level is greater than 1, so this URL path is the connection owner's, not a delegated agent's.
The owner grant minted from the catalog copies provider.operations into actions, which invoke then checks only by name.
Doppler's fence is the prefixes /v3/projects and /v3/configs/config/secrets/names.
doppler_promotion_is_value_blind requires allows_url to reject the literal secret-values path /v3/configs/config/secrets.
cloudflare-origin-ca is limited to /client/v4/certificates. The encoded ..%2f and %2e%2e%2f forms still match that prefix.
OpenRouter's path prefix is /api/v1/, so /api/v1/..%2fkeys still matches the segment-boundary test.
A custom connector's path prefix is the base URL path, so a base of https://host/api/v2 is supposed to confine the credential to that subtree.
The sibling path fence refuses dot segments, backslash, and semicolon in both the raw and percent-decoded path because the upstream's resolution is not the host's to predict.

blockers: The broker and reqwest 0.12.28 agree on the encoded request-target: try_uri parses url.as_str(), and a sandboxed url 2.5.8 parse kept paths such as /v3/projects/%2e%2e%2fconfigs/config/secrets, /client/v4/certificates/%2e%2e%2fuser/tokens/verify, and /api/v2/..%2fadmin. Reaching /v3/configs/config/secrets, /client/v4/user/tokens/verify, /keys, or a custom /admin path requires the upstream to percent-decode that target and then resolve .., backslash, or semicolon parameters. That behavior is not in the repository, and this sandbox has no external network, so api.doppler.com, api.cloudflare.com, and openrouter.ai were not called.

validation_plan.local: Call the crate EgressBinding::allows_url, not a transcribed copy. With Doppler's binding, https://api.doppler.com/v3/configs/config/secrets?project=a&config=b and https://api.doppler.com/v3/projects/%2e%2e/%2e%2e/configs/config/secrets must be Err, and https://api.doppler.com/v3/projects/%2e%2e%2fconfigs/config/secrets?project=a&config=b, https://api.doppler.com/v3/configs/config/secrets/names/..%2f..%2f?project=a&config=b, https://api.doppler.com/v3/projects/..;/configs/config/secrets, and https://api.doppler.com/v3/projects/%5c..%5cconfigs/config/secrets must be Ok. Repeat for Cloudflare Origin CA with https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/certificates/%2e%2e%2fuser/tokens/verify and for authority internal.example:8443 prefix /api/v2 with https://internal.example:8443/api/v2/..%2fadmin. Then, only on loopback, insert one Active in-org connection whose scheme is http, authority is 127.0.0.1, path_prefixes is [/api/v2], and bearer is a dummy value. Serve a fixture that records the raw request-target and whether that dummy bearer arrived, and returns 204. Invoke authorized_json GET http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/v2/..%2fadmin. The host side holds if the recorded target is still /api/v2/..%2fadmin and the dummy bearer is present. Do not treat that as proof a decoder maps it to /admin.
validation_plan.deployment:
Do not use a production token and do not store response bodies. With a non-production Cloudflare Origin CA token, compare only the HTTP status and top-level JSON keys of GET https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/certificates/%2e%2e%2fuser/tokens/verify to a direct GET of /client/v4/user/tokens/verify. If both are the token-verify success shape, the prefix did not hold. With a Doppler service token for a dummy project, compare only the status codes of GET https://api.doppler.com/v3/projects/%2e%2e%2fconfigs/config/secrets?project=

&config= and GET /v3/configs/config/secrets with the same query. Matching non-404 statuses means the values path was reached. Stop after that comparison.

title: Role evidence fence does not bind observation control or one-shot log reads
description: Browser observe tails re-read config_authorization_roles before releasing a sealed event: a missing row, a null role, or an auth_time that is not strictly after evidence_after ends the stream. That row is the Host membership ceiling provisioned for a sync pairing or device approval. set_role updates the ceiling and moves evidence_after forward, and on a null role deletes only project access; it does not revoke the browser client, stored authentication_json, in-memory session, or an authorized elevation. narrow_identity_role enforces the fence only when browser.authenticate is consumed, so a later step-up at or before the floor fails, but step_up keeps treating already stored phishing-resistant webauthn as fresh for 300 seconds. Control challenge, verify, commit, and control_with_host_authorization never read the row, so the same browser can mint or consume a handoff, take, or release elevation after the ceiling is cleared or the floor moves. GET /api/v1/agent/runs/{id}/log returns that run's sealed payloads after load(Attachment::View) and never calls StreamAuthority::active. NativeSession active reloads only the in-memory session. No gateway request of this sequence was executed.
claimed_root_cause: StreamAuthority::active enforces a non-null config_authorization_roles role and auth_time greater than evidence_after only for CredentialKind::BrowserGrant. step_up, agent.browser.control challenge and verify, control_with_host_authorization, NativeSession active, and read_log do not read that row. set_role_ceiling does not revoke browser clients, grants, stored authentication_json, sessions, or host elevations. narrow_identity_role applies the fence only to browser.authenticate.

trace.description: POST /api/v1/agent/runs/{id}/control loads the run as Attachment::Control, which calls step_up, then commits a take elevation. Handoff and release use the same commit path.

step_up is fresh only for a BrowserGrant with phishing-resistant webauthn, amr webauthn, and auth_time inside 300 seconds. Those claims come from stored authentication_json. The role ceiling and evidence_after floor are not read.
commit requires a BrowserGrant and a 64-hex elevation, hashes that elevation, and calls control_with_host_authorization. It does not read config_authorization_roles.
After the consume update matches, this statement writes control_state, quiescence, handoff_queued, lease holder, and lease expiry on the open run. Neither statement joins config_authorization_roles.

evidence.description: Browser active returns false when role_policy has a null role or when the reloaded grant auth_time is less than or equal to evidence_after. A missing policy row also returns false.
The NativeSession branch reloads only the in-memory session map and does not call role_policy.
step_up's freshness predicate is assurance, amr webauthn, and a 300-second auth_time window, with no role or evidence_after comparison.
The agent.browser.control challenge requires phishing-resistant assurance, an open run, and owner equality. It does not read config_authorization_roles.
narrow_identity_role runs only in the browser.authenticate branch. The agent.browser.control branch does not call it.

The consume UPDATE matches client, elevation digest, operation, target, transition, version, state, expiry, an unrevoked client, an unexpired grant, organization, and run owner. It does not join config_authorization_roles.
read_log authorizes with load(Attachment::View) and then reads observation events. It never calls StreamAuthority::active.
set_role calls set_role_ceiling with evidence_after set to the current timestamp. The handler does not revoke browser clients, grants, sessions, or host elevations.
A null role deletes that principal's config_project_access rows and appends a role_changed outbox event. It does not revoke browser grants or elevations.
session_claims copies assurance, auth_time, and the verified capability ceiling from stored authentication_json and does not read config_authorization_roles.

title: Windows open_url passes a Host authorization_url to cmd.exe /C start
description: connect create calls authorize_oauth for a configured oauth2_authorization_code connection that is not yet active. authorize_oauth takes the Host field authorization_url as a raw string and, unless --no-browser, passes it to open_url. open_url does not parse a scheme or reject command metacharacters. Its Windows branch is Command::new("cmd").arg("/C").arg("start").arg(url). start is a cmd.exe builtin, so the Host string is placed on a cmd command line rather than passed to a URL-only API. The broker's assert_transport_allowed allows only https, plus non-production loopback http, and only for URLs that crate builds; build_authorize_url then joins query pairs with raw &. Custom-provider https_url forbids a query and a fragment but not & in the path. The CLI never applies those checks: api() accepts any JSON object. The Host base URL is not loopback-only (default http://127.0.0.1:8787, overridable with --server or OPENSESAME_HOST_API). The architecture treats loopback as same-machine authority, which calibrates a purely local Host and does not cover a remote Host response used as a command line. This Linux host compiles the xdg-open arm, and cmd.exe was not executed. connect open reaches the same opener with a pages URL and is omitted so the trace has one entrypoint.
claimed_root_cause: The Windows arm of open_url is Command::new("cmd").arg("/C").arg("start").arg(url) with the Host authorization_url left unmodified. This crate adds no scheme allowlist, no empty start window title, and no cmd metacharacter escaping before Command::arg. The client treats the authorize JSON string as trusted and does not enforce the broker's https-or-nonproduction-loopback-http rule.

trace.description: The Host POST /api/v1/connections/{id}/authorize JSON field authorization_url is taken with as_str and is not parsed as a URL.
Unless --no-browser, which is a clap flag that defaults off, the raw authorization_url is passed to open_url.
When target_os is windows, the opener prefix is cmd, /C, start. macOS uses open and every other target uses xdg-open. The windows arm is not the branch compiled on this Linux host.
The Host string is appended with arg and the process is spawned. On Windows that command line is cmd.exe /C start followed by authorization_url.

evidence.description: authorization_url is required only to be a JSON string. No scheme, host, or metacharacter check follows before it is opened.
no_browser is a clap bool flag with no default_value, so the browser-open path is the default for connect create.
The Windows arm sets the argv prefix to cmd, /C, start and does not quote or filter the caller string in this function.
spawn uses Command::arg(url) and discards the result. This crate does not insert an empty start title or escape the string.
A non-empty Host body is serde_json::from_str into a Value, or a raw wrapper. AuthorizeResponseSchema is not applied.
The scheme match accepts https, and non-production loopback http, and rejects every other scheme. It does not inspect &.

append_pair starts the authorize query at response_type=code. The following pairs are client_id, redirect_uri, state, code_challenge, and code_challenge_method, so the serialized URL contains raw & separators.
This check rejects a custom authorize URL that already has a query or a fragment. It does not reject & in the path.
The Host API default address is http://127.0.0.1:8787.
The Host endpoint sets loopbackOnly to false, so the CLI is not pinned to a same-machine peer.

blockers: This host is Linux. cmd.exe and Wine are not installed, rust-src for the 1.88 toolchain is not installed, and cfg!(target_os = "windows") is false, so the compiled open_url branch is xdg-open. Windows CreateProcess quoting and cmd.exe parsing were not executed.

The decisive fact is whether cmd.exe /C start, given the single argument Rust Command::arg produces, treats a normal authorization_url that contains &, a path containing & around a command, or a non-URL command string, as more than one command. A Linux xdg-open result does not answer that.

validation_plan.local: On a Windows machine, in an empty temp directory, spawn only the same argv as open_url: Command::new("cmd").arg("/C").arg("start").arg(value), with no Host, no token, and no production server. Use a marker whose only effect is creating an empty file in that temp directory, then delete it. Test three values: (1) https://example.invalid/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=dummy ; (2) the marker command alone; (3) https://example.invalid/x&MARKER&y where MARKER is that create-file command and contains no further metacharacters. Record whether the marker file is created and whether cmd reports a second command. Do not change system settings or contact a real provider.
validation_plan.deployment: No production deployment, signing check, installer ACL, or device policy is required. A local Windows build of this CLI, or a throwaway copy of open_url, plus a stub authorization_url string, is enough.

title: Compose publishes the NATS client port with no host IP and no server auth config
description: ops/compose/docker-compose.yml is the file ops/README.md tells operators to start for local or HA-shaped runs. Its default-profile nats service uses image nats:2.11.4 and command ["-js", "-m", "8222"] with no volume, listen address, or authorization argument, then publishes container port 4222 as "4222:4222", which names no host IP. Monitoring port 8222 is not published. That service does not load ops/nats/local-dev.conf, whose comment says the plaintext profile authenticates nobody and must not be exposed beyond loopback, and whose listen directive is 127.0.0.1:4222. The same compose file sets gateway OPENSESAME_TASKBUS=nats and NATS_URL=nats://nats:4222 and sets no OPENSESAME_NATS_* variables. When those variables are unset, NatsTransportSpec::from_env returns None, create_nats uses NatsTransportSpec::plaintext, and it provisions because the profile is not secure. normalized() accepts a plaintext nats:// URL without requiring the dialed host to be loopback; on that branch it does refuse client identity, credentials, and tls_first. Stock gateway startup does not reach a connect: AppState::build calls StartupSecurity::load first, and from_env rejects this file because OPENSESAME_ENV and NODE_ENV are unset. The file also sets OPENSESAME_LISTEN=0.0.0.0:8787 and http://keycloak and http://gateway endpoints, which classify as networked, so a mode override would still hit the HTTPS safeguard, and assert_tcp_listen_allowed would still reject that listen without OPENSESAME_ALLOW_NONLOCAL=1. The worker service is behind the workload profile and does not set NATS_URL. Operator docs describe the compose client port as 4222 and show a host URL of nats://127.0.0.1:4222, which does not pin the published host IP. The file header calls the stack local/HA-capable and says to replace tags with digests in production; it does not label this publish as an accepted non-loopback exception. ops/README.md says to adapt the reference rather than adopt it wholesale, which also does not set the bind. Whether the unpinned Docker publish binds beyond loopback, and whether the nats:2.11.4 image accepts an unauthenticated client for this command, is not in the repository. Docker is not installed here and compose was not started.
claimed_root_cause: ops/compose/docker-compose.yml runs nats:2.11.4 with command ["-js", "-m", "8222"], no mounted authorization or listen config, and ports ["4222:4222"] with no host IP, instead of the 127.0.0.1 listener in ops/nats/local-dev.conf, and points the gateway task bus at nats://nats:4222 with no OPENSESAME_NATS_* settings.

The compose command is only ["-js", "-m", "8222"]. No config is mounted and no listen or authorization argument is set, so ops/nats/local-dev.conf is not applied. The image entrypoint that receives those arguments is not in this repository.

title: Shared startup denylist omits LD_AUDIT, so an env template loads an audit object in the credential-bearing child
description: credentialStartupEnvKeys is the only startup-hook denylist for both the TypeScript opensesame-id helper and the Rust opensesame password agent. It reserves LD_PRELOAD and LD_LIBRARY_PATH and does not reserve glibc LD_AUDIT. An environment template is lower-trust input: the operator chooses the command, and the template is supposed to be rejected when it names an interpreter or dynamic-linker hook. validateRunTemplate, assertSafeRunName, and the Rust validate_run_template and validate_run_assignments consult only that list, so a literal LD_AUDIT assignment is accepted and passed through as op run --env-file. helperEnvironment and scrub_startup remove only listed names. On the TypeScript path the provider child is a node wrapper whose script deletes OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN only after the dynamic linker has started the process. On the Rust path Env::Run forwards the same unrejected bytes, authenticate() may then place the service token on the op command, and internal_exec removes that token only when it starts the selected command. A glibc parent that was itself started under LD_AUDIT is already running the library before either scrub; that inherited case is not a separate boundary. The boundary the denylist exists to enforce is introduction of the hook by the template. The same omitted key is not a second fingerprint. The name check also accepts an LD_AUDIT=op:// assignment, but the executed load used a literal path in the template.
root_cause: spec/conformance/2password-policy.json credentialStartupEnvKeys omits LD_AUDIT, and both the TypeScript and Rust password-agent gates treat that shared list as the complete set of reserved startup hooks.
intended_behavior: Interpreter and dynamic-linker startup hooks are reserved before credential-bearing helpers run. Inherited hooks are removed before authentication, and run assignments and environment templates cannot introduce them. The selected child receives ordinary resolved variables only after the provider service token is removed. ADR 0177 states this for both CLI adapters.

trace.description: env run reads the caller-supplied template and passes its text to the password-agent runFile path. The template is the lower-trust input; the child command is a separate argument.
runFile calls validateRunTemplate and, on success, forwards the same contents to the host runEnvFile port. A literal LD_AUDIT assignment is not rejected.
Each parsed assignment name is passed to assertSafeRunName, which rejects only an uppercase match in credentialStartupEnvKeys. LD_AUDIT is accepted.
LD_PRELOAD is reserved in this array. The array also lists LD_LIBRARY_PATH and does not contain LD_AUDIT. The TypeScript policy import and the Rust include_str both compile this file.
The accepted template is written unchanged to an owner-only snapshot and supplied as op run --env-file. Nothing removes LD_AUDIT from those bytes.

op is spawned with helperEnvironment, which still holds the service token and does not remove an unlisted LD_AUDIT. The provider applies the env file to the node wrapper. The wrapper script at line 151 deletes OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN only after the dynamic linker has loaded LD_AUDIT.

evidence.description: The credentialStartupEnvKeys array includes LD_PRELOAD and LD_LIBRARY_PATH and has no LD_AUDIT entry. It contains 18 names and ends at DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS.
The TypeScript password-agent policy is this JSON file, so the CLI helper and the app-core validators share the incomplete list.
assertSafeRunName throws only when the uppercase name is a member of credentialStartupEnvKeys.
helperEnvironment deletes only names whose uppercase form is in credentialStartupEnvKeys. OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN is not in that list and is kept.
The fixed node wrapper deletes OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN in JavaScript after the process has started.
authenticatedPort merges the service-account environment into runEnvFile before the snapshot is executed, which is how the wrapper receives the token.
The repository op run stand-in copies the parent environment, overlays every env-file KEY=value line, substitutes op:// values, and spawnSyncs the wrapper with that environment.
The Rust policy is include_str of the same JSON, so the Rust password agent uses the same incomplete key list.
credential_startup_key matches a name only by eq_ignore_ascii_case against credential_startup_env_keys.
validate_run_template rejects an assignment only when credential_startup_key is true, so a literal LD_AUDIT line is kept.
scrub_startup env_removes each policy name and, in the following loop, only current names for which credential_startup_key is true. Unlisted LD_AUDIT is not removed.
When the parent environment holds a service-account token, authenticate() copies it onto the helper command after startup scrubbing.
This argument passes the unchanged template snapshot to op run --env-file. The snapshot is not filtered to drop LD_AUDIT.
internal_exec removes OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN from the selected command and does not remove LD_AUDIT. That removal runs only after internal-exec itself has started.
Both CLI adapters are required to reserve interpreter startup variables before provider execution and to remove inherited startup hooks before authenticating.

conditions.description: The operator runs env run, or the Rust password-agent env run, on a template the attacker can influence. The child command is chosen separately from the template.

The template contains a literal LD_AUDIT assignment whose value is a path to an attacker-controlled glibc audit object, and a service-account token is present in the helper environment. The parent process is not itself started under LD_AUDIT.

The credential child is a dynamically linked ELF started by glibc, which loads LD_AUDIT and calls la_version before main. This was observed with Node v22.23.3 on Linux. macOS dyld and Windows do not honor LD_AUDIT; their listed equivalents are already denied.

The provider applies env-file assignments to the child and forwards the parent environment. That is what packages/cli/src/fixtures/password-agent/op.cjs does for op run, which is the provider stand-in used by this repository.

execution.attacker_perspective: An author of an environment template supplies a literal LD_AUDIT assignment naming a shared object they control, next to an ordinary op:// reference. The operator runs that template through the credential helper, which is supposed to reject startup hooks such as LD_PRELOAD and NODE_OPTIONS before the service token is exposed.
instructions: Build a local glibc shared object that exports la_version and whose constructor records only whether LD_AUDIT is set and whether OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN equals the dummy value ops_canary.
Read credentialStartupEnvKeys from spec/conformance/2password-policy.json.

In the approved sandbox, call validateRunTemplate, assertSafeRunName, and helperEnvironment from the TypeScript password-agent sources on a template containing the op:// line and the literal LD_AUDIT line, and on the LD_PRELOAD and NODE_OPTIONS controls.

Copy packages/cli/src/fixtures/password-agent/op.cjs to an absolute PATH directory other than the process cwd, set PARITY_DB and PARITY_LOG, and call runEnvFileSnapshot with that template, options.env OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN=ops_canary, and a child command of node -e process.exit(0). Do not start the parent with LD_AUDIT.

Separately, exec a dynamically linked ELF after removing the dummy token and every name that case-insensitively matches the policy list, which is the scrub_startup rule, and compare it with a preload-only run after the same removal and with an unsanitized LD_PRELOAD control.
Stop after the marker lines. Do not use a real service-account token or continue into the selected command.
execution.observed_result: The policy contained 18 keys, included LD_PRELOAD, and did not contain LD_AUDIT. validateRunTemplate accepted the LD_AUDIT template and rejected LD_PRELOAD and NODE_OPTIONS. assertSafeRunName accepted ld_audit. helperEnvironment kept LD_AUDIT and ops_canary and removed LD_PRELOAD and NODE_OPTIONS. The parent process did not have LD_AUDIT. runEnvFileSnapshot against the repository op fixture exited 0. The audit object recorded ctor saw_canary=1 has_ld_audit=1 and la_version in the node wrapper, then ctor saw_canary=0 has_ld_audit=1 and la_version in the grandchild after the wrapper deleted the token. A separate exec that removed only those 18 names and the dummy token kept LD_AUDIT, and that glibc child called la_version and its constructor. The same removal applied to LD_PRELOAD alone did not load the object. An unsanitized LD_PRELOAD control ran the constructor and did not call la_version. The reproduction called those TypeScript functions directly, with the dummy token supplied the way authenticatedPort attaches it. The Rust opensesame binary was not executed.

remediation.strategy: Add LD_AUDIT to credentialStartupEnvKeys. The TypeScript validators and helperEnvironment and the Rust validators and scrub_startup all read this list, so one entry reserves the hook in templates, assignment names, and helper environments. The node wrapper cannot delete the service token before the dynamic linker runs, so the variable must be rejected and stripped before exec. Extend the existing startup-key regression, which already iterates the shared list, to require that LD_AUDIT is rejected in the same case variants as LD_PRELOAD and removed before authenticate() attaches a token.

likelihood.reason: The operator must run env run or the Rust password-agent env run on an attacker-influenced template that names a loadable glibc audit object. That is ordinary local or repository input on Linux, and it is the same class of input the existing NODE_OPTIONS and LD_PRELOAD denylist already treats as in scope. It is not a remote anonymous request.

impact.reason: The audit object runs inside the node wrapper while the dummy service-account token is still in the environment, and it runs again in the selected child after that token is deleted. Code in that position can disclose the service token and provider-injected variables and can execute as that process.

confidence.reason: The omission is a direct membership test over the shared JSON, and a sandboxed run of the cited TypeScript validators and runEnvFileSnapshot against the repository op fixture called la_version while the dummy token was still set. The Rust adapter's use of the same list, its unchanged env-file forwarding, and its post-start token removal were read from source; a glibc exec after removing only the listed names also called la_version. The Rust binary itself was not run.

title: In-flight runner keeps filling an origin after its arm expires when getRun names another armed origin
description: driveRun opens the page and vault context for the run id and origin taken from listRuns, then before every later claim applies skipReason to whatever getRun returns. getAgentRun returns a decoded body without requiring its id or origin to be the requested run, while claim, settle, and fill keep using the opened run. skipReason therefore applies the arm, grant, and credential checks to the body origin, and fill_credential still resolves the opened origin's password. Options-page Stop calls service.disarm, which also revokes the browser grant, so that path is outside this window. Arm expiry is inside it: isArmed is false once expiresAt passes, but lapse revokes the grant only at the start of a tick, and a tick started while driveRun is in progress is the same pass. A getRun body whose origin is another still-ready origin keeps skipReason successful, so this pass does not return and the opened origin's password is written while its grant is still held. After the pass returns, the next tick's lapse does revoke that grant. The checked-in gateway copies stored target_origin, and no update in this repository rewrites that column, so an unmodified gateway does not flip the field. The failing input is a non-conforming response from the loopback Host the extension is already calling.
root_cause: The fresh Host view is not bound to the run id and origin the page was opened for. getAgentRun returns the decoded body id and origin without comparing them to the requested id, and driveRun uses that body only for skipReason while the vault context, claim, and settle keep the original run.
intended_behavior: A claim is authorized only for the same run id and origin whose page was opened. When that origin is no longer armed, the runner claims nothing further and does not write that origin's credential.

trace.description: getRun forwards getAgentRun's decoded Host body for the opened run id into the runner and does not compare that body to the requested id or to the origin already being driven.
The decoded view is returned whenever it is shaped like a run. Its id and origin are the body fields, not the id in the request path.
skipReason is applied to that fresh view before every claim. The DriverDeps created at open still name the original run id, origin, tab, and vault context.
The arm, browser grant, and credential checks use current.origin from the Host body. They do not use the origin stored on the open page.
fill_credential resolves current_password for the opened context origin and pages.fill writes that value into the page that was opened for it.

evidence.description: The execution context fixes run.id and run.origin when the page is opened and is not updated from later Host views.
After skipReason passes, claim is issued for the opened run id, not for the id in the fresh view.
answer executes the claimed step with the DriverDeps and the AgentRunView captured at open, not with the fresh Host view. settle then uses that same opened run id.
decodeAgentRun copies id and origin from the JSON object and does not know which run was requested.
decodeClaim rejects a body whose run_id is not the requested run id. getAgentRun has no equivalent bind, so only the authorization view can name a different run.
Expired arms are disarmed and their grants revoked only in lapse, which runTick calls before driveRun and not again until that pass finishes.
tick shares one in-flight pass, so a later alarm cannot enter lapse while driveRun is still claiming steps.
armed() omits a row once expiresAt is no longer in the future, so isArmed becomes false without deleting the row or revoking the grant.
service.disarm, which the options-page Stop message calls, removes the arm and revokes the grant together. The expiry window inside driveRun does not take that path.
The production page port passes the fill value to the injected pfFill. It does not consult the fresh Host origin; the tab origin was fixed when the page was opened.
pfFill writes the value it was given into the matched field. That value is the opened origin's credential, not a credential for the origin named by the later getRun body.
The gateway run view sets origin from the stored target_origin of the row loaded by the path id.
Control updates rewrite control state, quiescence, handoff, and lease fields, not target_origin. The column is written at insert and is not reassigned by any update in this repository.

conditions.description: The extension already holds a Host session and has opened a drive for origin A from listRuns while A was armed, granted, and credentialed.
Some other origin B remains armed, browser-granted, and present in the vault, and a recovery recipient and private-window permission are still set, so a view naming B passes skipReason.

A's arm expires during driveRun, so isArmed(A) is false while lapse has not run again and A's host permission is still held. An options-page Stop revokes the grant immediately and is outside this window. After this pass returns, the next tick's lapse revokes the grant.

The loopback Host the extension is calling returns a getRun body whose origin is not the opened run, with expires_at still ahead of the runner clock. The in-repo gateway serializes the stored target_origin for the path id and does not update that column.

execution.attacker_perspective: A process that can answer as the loopback Host the runner is already calling returns, after the page is open, a run view for a different id and for origin B while the page and vault context remain origin A, and A's arm expires during that pass.
instructions: Arm https://rp.example for a short TTL and https://other.example for longer, grant both, store a distinct credential for each, pin a recovery recipient, and allow a private window.

List one agent-driving run whose id is run:1 and whose origin is https://rp.example, with expires_at still ahead of the runner clock, and queue navigate to that origin, fill_credential of current_password, and submit.
On the first getRun, return that same run. On later getRun calls, move only the settings clock past https://rp.example's expiresAt, leave its browser grant in place, and return the payload above.
Repeat with getRun still returning id run:1 and origin https://rp.example after the same clock advance.
execution.observed_result: With the swapped body, the runner opened run:1 on https://rp.example, claimed only run:1, and settled navigate, fill_credential, and submit. The fill port received https://rp.example's vault password and not https://other.example's, while isArmed(https://rp.example) was false, https://other.example stayed armed, and the grant for https://rp.example was still held. A second tick() during that pass was the same promise. With the origin left unchanged, the runner settled only navigate, skipped run:1 as not_armed, and did not fill or submit. In both cases a later tick then revoked the https://rp.example grant.

remediation.strategy: Before skipReason, reject a fresh view whose id or origin differs from the run the page was opened for, and do not claim. The arm check then stays on that same origin, so expiry makes driveRun return and the next tick can lapse the grant. Also reject a getAgentRun body whose id is not the requested id. Add a regression that expires only the opened origin and swaps the getRun origin after the first step, expecting no further claim, and keep the case where an unchanged origin stops with not_armed.

likelihood.reason: The host base is loopback-pinned, and the in-repo gateway returns the stored target_origin for the path id without any update of that column. A drive also cannot start for an origin that fails skipReason on listRuns. The extension has to be talking to a Host that misreports a later getRun, some other origin must still pass skipReason, and the opened origin's arm must expire during that in-flight pass. A normal Stop click revokes the grant and is not this window.

impact.reason: After the opened origin is no longer armed, the runner still writes that origin's current password into the page it already opened and can submit it, and this pass does not revoke the host permission. The password is not returned to the Host or taken from the other origin. The grant is revoked on the next tick once the pass returns, including when the step queue goes idle.

confidence.reason: The repository runner, readiness, settings, vault, and driver code was executed both with a swapped getRun body and with the origin unchanged, using an arm clock moved past expiresAt rather than settings.disarm. The swapped body filled and submitted the opened origin's password; the unchanged origin stopped with not_armed and did not fill. Tick coalescing and grant revocation on the following tick were observed. Gateway serialization of target_origin was read from source.
